headline: Highest risk is medium: Continue can read/write shared workspace files while ComfyUI exposes model files and offline queues, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and can use MCP/tooling, while ComfyUI exposes files and an asynchronous queue system. If ComfyUI outputs are copied into Continue or shared files are parsed as instructions, injected content can steer downstream behavior. The pathway is plausible in default shared-workspace setups, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated text or metadata is placed in a workspace file that Continue reads
IF Continue is configured to treat shared files or MCP-fed content as instructions
mitigations: Separate ComfyUI output folders from Continue workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of generated text into prompts
Require manual review before copying model outputs into Continue
Use a read-only handoff directory
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and may send content to a chosen model provider or MCP server; ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts. In a shared workspace, sensitive assets can flow from ComfyUI into Continue prompts or logs, creating a default leakage path unless the operator isolates files.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in the same workspace Continue indexes or opens
IF Continue is pointed at a remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep media/model artifacts outside the IDE workspace
Use local-only models for Continue
Restrict Continue to a dedicated project folder
Review prompt logs before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACL separation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, read/write filesystem, and broad network egress; ComfyUI can also write files and runs an asynchronous queue system. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent writes and state changes can corrupt artifacts or overwrite outputs. The shared-filesystem concurrency path is explicit in Continue and dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same workspace or model directory
IF Continue issues file writes while ComfyUI queue jobs are producing outputs
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Pause one agent during the other's write-heavy tasks
Enable filesystem backups or snapshots
Avoid git operations in the shared workspace
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on model outputs via chat, autocomplete, shell, and MCP, while ComfyUI produces generated content that may be treated as authoritative by the operator. If ComfyUI output is copied into Continue without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or tool actions. Continue's approval gate reduces but does not eliminate this risk.
conditions: IF ComfyUI output is pasted into Continue prompts or tasks
IF Continue is allowed to execute shell or MCP actions after that input
mitigations: Verify generated content before reuse
Require human review for any action derived from model output
Keep Continue tool approval enabled
Use a checklist for code or command changes
requires-engineering: add validation between generation and action

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch shown. The main compliance concern is operational: Continue can send workspace content to a chosen provider, while ComfyUI handles media/model artifacts locally. Without a documented mismatch, only a small compliance gap is evident.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Continue and routed to a noncompliant provider
IF ComfyUI artifacts contain restricted data and are copied into Continue logs
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces
Use local providers for Continue
Audit retention settings on the model provider
Separate sensitive projects from general use
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls
